content.text: No MFN obligation on Customer exists anywhere in the document; § 12.3 expressly disclaims one, and the pricing sections (7.1, 8.3) impose obligations only on Vendor.

input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or most-favoured-customer obligation running from Customer to Vendor. Section 12.3 expressly confirms Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, and there is no disclosure, benchmarking, or right-to-match mechanic anywhere (searches for "most-favoured", "favourable/favorable", "match", "first refusal", and benchmarking language returned nothing else). The pricing provisions run the other way in our favour: § 7.1 fixes Fees during the initial term and bars unstated charges, and § 8.3 caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and three percent, both obligations on Vendor only. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN), so no redline is proposed.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
